newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.C sells $140 mln of bonds to retail so far.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.C sells $140 mln of bonds to retail so far.

text.p: New York City, which on Wednesday expects to issue nearly $1 billion of debt, on Monday said that during the second day of its presale period for retail investors it sold another $40 million of bonds.

"I think we're well pleased," said a New York City official, who declined to be named. He noted that the market was subdued on the day before the November 5 presidential elections, and that the total now sold to retail investors adds up to around $140 million.
The retail order period ends on Tuesday at 1600 EST, and the city typically sells around $200 million to individual investors.
Two maturities on Friday sold out, the 2000 and 2001 maturities, with the first one fetching a 4.75 percent yield, which matches its coupon, and the 2001 at five percent.
The retail scale, which typically is priced more agressively than what later is offered to institutions, ranges from the 4.75 percent yield on the 2000 bonds to 6.18 percent for 2026.
